cohorts.subjects: Cadaveric human thoracic spines (the abstract calls them donors): 72 isolated motion segments, each two vertebrae with the disc between, from 30 spines, six segments per disc level C7-T1 to T11-T12; dissected free of soft tissue, ribs sawn off, stored frozen at -28 deg C. Inclusion: only segments with mild or moderate degeneration (grades ii and iii of the authors' four-grade scheme) on anatomical and radiographic inspection; radiographs with overlay or poor film quality excluded. Country, collection, ethnicity, stature and cause of death are not stated. Inference: the specimens were probably obtained in Germany, since the authors work at the University of Ulm. Discs were not grouped by age or sex for analysis; the sex split per level is not given.
cohorts.n_units: 72 thoracic motion segments (6 per disc level, C7-T1 to T11-T12) of 30 spines; vertebral bodies C7 to T12, n per body not printed
cohorts.ages: female mean 58.67 +/- 10.74, range 43-80 years; male mean 56.20 +/- 11.65, range 37-79 years; all 57.43 +/- 11.27 years
cohorts.sexes: 15 female donors (37 segments), 15 male donors (35 segments)

cohorts.subjects: Todd and Pyle's (1928) anatomical series, used as outside test data for this paper's equations (Fig 9b,c; the Results text also names it for Fig 9a, whose legend says present study). The Introduction says Todd and Pyle used only male cadavers and did not report the age distribution; nothing else about the subjects is given.
cohorts.n_units: not stated; plotted at T1 to T12

cohorts.subjects: Pooni et al. (1986): a few elderly cadavers aged 73 to 85 years, cited in the Introduction; their data were given only as a percentage of total spine height. Sex and number not stated.

techniques.instrument: sliding vernier caliper (Mitutoyo Absolute Digimatic); high-precision saw (Exacta, PSI Medical); saw microtome (Leica SP4000)
techniques.how: Frozen segments cut horizontally through both bodies, posterior elements removed; two rods (3.0 mm by 20 mm) set into each body to mark the frontal and median sagittal planes; the segment frozen in an ice block and cut sagittally along the rods. On the mid-sagittal section ADH and PDH taken between the anterior and posterior end-plate landmarks and MDH between two mid-vertebral points on the superior and inferior end-plates, cartilaginous end-plates included. Gives the anatomical ADH, PDH and MDH of Table 1 and the disc values of Tables 3 and 4.
techniques.magnification: none; measured directly on the specimen
techniques.observers: two observers measured every specimen (inter-observer CV 0.79-0.93 for disc heights); the Results call the intra-observer errors (1.7-6.1% ADH, 17-26.1% PDH, 1.7-5.1% VBHA and VBHP) anatomical, but the Methods put the repeats on 10 radiographs and the body heights exist only on film, so the mapped reading files them under lateral_contact_radiograph (Inference)

techniques.instrument: Faxitron automatic X-ray machine (Hewlett Packard); electronic digital caliper (Mitutoyo Absolute Digimatic, +/- 0.05 mm) on the film
techniques.how: Each isolated segment radiographed in a neutral standard position, film-focus distance 60 cm, 60 s, 46.5 kV, beam centred on the disc; on a viewing table eight landmarks, the anterior and posterior corners of the end-plates of both vertebrae, marked by Farfan's method; ADH and PDH between the corners across the disc, VBHA and VBHP between the corners of each body (cartilaginous end-plates not counted). No radiographic MDH. Antero-posterior films were also taken, but no AP measurement is reported. Gives the radiographic columns of Table 1 and all of Table 2.
techniques.magnification: corrected: films calibrated by a scale on the rig close to the specimen, and a factor calculated for the error of off-centre positioning
techniques.observers: two observers measured every radiograph (inter-observer CV 0.49-0.82 for disc heights, 0.49 for PDH, 0.95-0.98 for VBHA and VBHP); intra-observer repeats on 10 radiographs of 10 specimens at five levels

techniques.instrument: calculation from the level means of Tables 1 and 2
techniques.how: Indices I1 = (ADH + PDH)/(VBHA + VBHP), I2 = MDH/(ADH + PDH), I3 = ADH/PDH and the disc : body ratio 1/I1 (Table 3); linear and polynomial (up to cubic) least-squares fits of disc and body heights on ADH, VBHA and VBHP, ANOVA for significance (Table 4, Figs 2 and 6 to 8); the equations then applied to Todd and Pyle's data (Fig 9). Inference: the fits are across the 12 disc-level or 13 vertebral-level means, not across specimens (Fig 2's caption says level means).
techniques.magnification: not applicable; inherits the radiographic correction
techniques.page: p. 377 (PDF 3); Table 3 p. 379 (PDF 5); Table 4 p. 382 (PDF 8); Figs 6-9 pp. 383-386 (PDF 9-12)

techniques.how: Todd and Pyle's own anatomical measurements of VBHA and VBHP (and ADH, Fig 4a), as they published them; this paper describes no landmarks or plane for them.

within_paper: One cohort measured twice: every one of the 72 segments was measured both directly on its mid-sagittal section and on its lateral radiograph (p. 377, PDF 3), so Table 1's anatomical and radiographic columns, Table 2's radiographic body heights and the derived Table 3, Table 4 and Figs 2, 3 and 6 to 8 all come from the same 72 segments of 30 donors; the female (37 segments, 15 donors) and male (35 segments, 15 donors) counts are parts of it, not separate cohorts. Inference: each of T1 to T11 is the lower body of one segment type and the upper body of the next, so a Table 2 row may pool bodies from two segment types, and the pictured T9-T10 segment of a 57-year-old woman (Fig 1, p. 376, PDF 2) is presumably one of the 72. Fig 9a's points are this study's by its legend while the Results text (p. 381, PDF 7) attributes them to Todd and Pyle.
